what: Release 1 of the main chart (issue #31): the singularity chart, tested (hero), the calendar view and McKenna's timewave. Observed data, published tables and the registered tests only.
rules: No fitted date anywhere except the track record: there, only refits whose registry row has a display_approved_pr (the owner's waiver of 2026-10-24, #31; skeptic review pending), each shown with the 95% range it claimed at that refit (a past claim), a passed one marked as a failed forecast.

No axis measured from a fitted date and no clock running down to any date, with one exception (the owner's, #31): the single line under the omega card that gives the days from today to the card's date, next to the same count at the previous refit, both from display-approved track-record rows. One fitted curve: the hero's best-fit curve (quadratic in the log of the time left, #80), aimed at the omega card's date: solid up to today, then dashed after today down to that date, where the fitted wait reaches zero (owner's request, #31). The steps chart draws no curve (owner's request, #80).
No data curve after the last observed release; the one extrapolation is that best-fit curve, dashed after today.

After today: only the two registered CVE test windows, the track record's display-approved dates, the omega card's 50% range as a band with the best-fit curve dashed down to the card's date (the hero; the steps chart shows the band and the date only), and, if the reader switches it there, McKenna's timewave with its zero moved to the omega card's date (a formula placed by a fitted estimate).
Every estimate and lower bound is marked in the drawing.

releases.definition: Non-minor rows (minor == False) of results/releases_all_labs/all_labs_included_labeled.csv: 855 rows from 199 labs. Same rule as the release panels below.
releases.event_rule: A release event is one (lab, date) pair: same-day non-minor releases from one lab are one event.
releases.gap_rule: gap_any_lab_next_days = days to the next later release date from any lab (pooled); gap_same_lab_next_days = days to the same lab's next later release date; null = none in the snapshot.
releases.label: All releases · 199 labs
releases.coverage_note: Epoch's catalogue covers more labs in recent years, so part of the shrinking wait is wider coverage, not faster progress. The test that separates the two is registered and not run yet.
releases.lag_note: Epoch lag: recent counts are lower bounds, recent gaps upper bounds.
releases.lag_zone_rule: the all-labs freeze's lag cutoff: the snapshot date minus 60 days (results/releases_all_labs/RULES.md). A gap that ends inside the zone is drawn hollow, as an upper bound.

pace.unit: days (wait between new AI models); one value per calendar day, days[i]
pace.first_day_rule: first day whose 90-day window lies wholly inside the coverage (coverage_from + 89 days)
pace.last_day_rule: the line ends at the last listed release: nothing is drawn after the last observed release
pace.sparse_note: days whose window holds fewer than 8 counted release events are drawn dim (few releases: the wait swings with each one)

definition.per_lab: wait_per_lab[d] = lab_days[d] / n_lab[d]. lab_days[d] = the sum over the 90 days d-89..d of the number of labs active that day (provisional entry dates). n_lab[d] = release events dated d-89..d, not counting each lab's own entry event (it starts the lab's clock). Reads: on average each active lab released one new model every wait_per_lab days. null when n_lab = 0.
definition.pooled: wait_pooled[d] = 90 / n_all[d]; n_all[d] = all release events dated d-89..d (all labs pooled, raw, entry events included). Reads: one new model from any of the labs every wait_pooled days. Part of its 2022-24 fall is labs entering the list, not faster releases. null when n_all = 0.

pace.down_means: a shorter wait, i.e. more novelty (down = more novelty, as in the timewave)

scales.note: fixed log y-ranges, chosen once to contain every value (min x 0.82, max x 1.25); they never change with zoom

none_spans.definition: runs of days whose 90-day window holds no counted release event (wait undefined); drawn as gaps marked 'no release'

drops.definition: A drop ends on day d when the plotted wait fell over the 30 days d-30..d: size = ln(wait[d-30]) - ln(wait[d]), both defined. Kept if size >= ln(1.3), the window at d holds at least 8 counted release events, and no day within 35 days has a larger size (ties go to the earlier day). Ranked by size, largest first, ties by date. releases = indices into releases.rows dated in (d-30, d]; entering = labs whose provisional entry falls in (d-30, d]; such a drop is labelled '<lab> enters the list' instead of by its releases.
drops.name_rule: Label names: one name per release event in (d-30, d], chosen by a written rule from releases.rows only (no hand-picked list is consulted). Events are ordered by: closed weights first; then more models released together by the lab that day; then the later date; then the shorter name. Each event is named by its closed-weight model first, then its shortest name.
drops.names_status: placeholder names, not causes: which releases explain each drop is still being checked
drops.label_rule: Drops are labelled in rank order, each shortened to fit (two names, one name, then the count of releases); a name is never cut mid-word. If even the count does not fit, labelling stops: a lower-ranked drop is never labelled in its place.
drops.missing_note: GPT-4 and GPT-4 Turbo are not in the non-minor series (their Epoch names carry a month-year suffix), so no label can name them (issue #31, release-tracker).

heldout.question: Which fit scored the next gap better?
heldout.measure: mean error = mean |ln(predicted next gap / actual next gap)|; lower is better; 0 = perfect
heldout.measure_src: scripts/part8.py lines 28-45 (rolling origin: predict each next gap from the releases before it)
heldout.copied: Only n and the two mean errors per list are copied, from lines 8 (v1) and 11 (v3); nothing else in the file is used. registered_tests.unit: records with cveMetadata.state == PUBLISHED, binned by UTC datePublished (as scripts/cve/count.py)
registered_tests.what_cve_is: CVE records are public reports of software security flaws.
registered_tests.why_here: The project registered these two counts in advance to test the stored CVE models, singular and non-singular, both ways.
registered_tests.two_sided: Both tests are two-sided: a low count refutes stored hyperbola (singular) fits; a high count refutes non-singular models whose upper 95% bound it exceeds.
registered_tests.scoring_plain: Each test is scored on the first cvelistV5 release published after its window has closed (rule in the registration file).
registered_tests.rule_texts: copied verbatim from the registration, except a clause quoting a fitted date, which is withheld
registered_tests.caption_status: plain wording carried from the reviewed R1b prototype; final wording is Skeptic's and signals-analyst's (issue #31)
registered_tests.left_out: Per-model forecasts and ranges in the same file are not copied, so nothing forecast can be drawn; scoring dates are not copied.

test1.question: Late-October count over every whole UTC day from the day after the PR opens through 2026-10-31
test1.rule_below: count < threshold refutes the [fitted date withheld] fits (hyp|2023-01, hyp|2024-07)
test1.rule_at_or_above: count >= threshold: those fits survive Test 1 and every non-singular model whose Test 1 hi95 is below the count is refuted; this approves no date
test1.caption: Fewer than 4,741 new CVE records refutes two stored hyperbola fits (hyp|2023-01, hyp|2024-07).
test1.caption_otherwise: At or above it, those two fits survive, and any non-singular model whose upper 95% bound is below the count is refuted; that approves no date.
test1.withheld: a clause quoting a fitted date (binding rule: no fitted date on the site)

test2.question: Full November 2026 total
test2.rule: count < lower edge refutes every stored hyperbola; lower edge..midpoint inconclusive (reported as such); >= midpoint: hyperbolas not refuted and every non-singular model (exp, quad, kink, step [fixed 2026-08-25 break], logistic) whose Test 2 hi95 is below the count is refuted. hyp|2023-01 and hyp|2024-07 are undefined [fitted date withheld]: any finite count refutes them. The raw count decides; the dip-adjusted value is reported only.
test2.caption: Fewer than 27,986 refutes every stored hyperbola; 27,986 to 31,975 is inconclusive.
test2.caption_otherwise: At 31,975 or more the stored hyperbolas are not refuted, and any non-singular model (exp, quad, kink, step, logistic) whose upper 95% bound is below the count is refuted; that approves no date.
test2.always_refuted: hyp|2023-01 and hyp|2024-07 are refuted by any November count, as registered.
test2.withheld: a clause quoting a fitted date (binding rule: no fitted date on the site)

timewave.label: McKenna's timewave (a formula, not data)
timewave.caption: McKenna's timewave (a formula, not data). Terence & Dennis McKenna's King Wen "novelty" curve (The Invisible Landscape, 1975; Kelley set, Peter Meyer's Timewave Zero). McKenna ended it on 2012-12-21. Shown for shape only: unfitted to data, silent on the future. Here it ends on the omega point (a fitted estimate) when the card names a date; otherwise the omega view stays blank. You can pick his date instead; its lows are placed by a fitted date and say nothing about what will happen: a formula, not predicted events.
timewave.caption_src: issue #31: timewave-historian proposal, skeptic-red-team approved; condensed 2026-10-24 by the owner's copy edit (reviewed by the director), replacing the longer approved string (the book title is italic); #84
credit_lines: Timewave theory: Terence McKenna and Dennis McKenna, The Invisible Landscape (1975).
Number set: Kelley. Software and mathematics: Peter Meyer, fractal-timewave.com.
timewave.credit_lines_src: issue #31: credit lines approved by skeptic-red-team; 'Number set: Kelley' until Meyer's own page is cited for Kelley and Taylor
timewave.anchor_src: scripts/timewave.py line 76 (ZERO: 06:00 Colombia time, the Timewave Zero software default)
timewave.anchor_rule: The curve opens with its zero on the omega point, the card's fitted estimate (refit weekly), when the card names a date; otherwise the omega view stays blank. Each low after today is then placed by that estimate, moves with it day for day, and is labelled (formula, est.). The McKenna's 2012 button puts the zero back on his own date, 2012-12-21; no low is then drawn after today. Nothing is drawn after the zero; today is marked.

lows.rule: A low is a day, 14 to 365 days before the end date, whose formula value (at 00:00 UTC) is the smallest within 10 days on either side and which the curve rises from, on both sides within that window, by at least a factor of 10^0.1.
lows.list_note: (formula, est.). They sit a fixed number of days before the end date, so they move with every weekly refit. Whether they line up with anything has not been tested.

timewave.number_set: Kelley (TIL 1975 Table 2), data/kelley/kelley_TIL_table2.txt; entry 119 = 22 (DEFINITIONS.md section 6). 32 (WEN_GRPH) is a sensitivity check and is not drawn.
timewave.code: scripts/timewave.py Timewave(data, wf=64)(days before the anchor): Meyer's fractal transform, / 64^3
timewave.y_note: novelty value: lower = more novel (McKenna's convention). Unitless. Own fixed scale.
timewave.sampling: Sampled, not exact: 3371 log-spaced samples before 1900 (2000 per decade, out to 5475 years before the anchor), daily values at 00:00 UTC from 1900-01-01, then 1986 log-spaced samples within 64 days before the anchor (400 per decade), generated by scripts/timewave_export.py. Exact evaluation at every zoom is #16.
timewave.no_claim: No claim that dips line up with events: that is McKenna's claim, and it has not been tested here.

events.legend: events McKenna linked to the wave (his picks)
events.anchor_legend: the anchor of McKenna's own calculation (Hiroshima + 24,576 days = November 2012), not a match
events.rule: McKenna's own picks: past events he linked to the wave after the fact; nobody registered the list in advance. One row is a caption he printed in 1987 before the date it names, shown as his forecast, not as an event. The anchor of his own calculation is shown apart and counted with none of them. Drawn at their real dates under either end date the panel offers. His sources do not agree on one last day for the wave: each event shows the one its own source states. Nothing is scored and the wave's bumps are not tested against them (that test is #20, not run). Captions are shown as his figure captions, not as speech; a quote cut from a sentence is shown after a leading ellipsis; the sources were checked against the originals (#31).

No event was added. track_record.lede: Each row is one refit of the same fixed method on the selected list of hand-picked models: the date the fit named then (a fitted estimate) and the 95% range it claimed at that refit (a past claim, not the card's range). Hollow points mark dates that have passed (failed forecasts). These dates form a track record, not a forecast; each series' verdict is the status label in the Series status section of the Learn page.
track_record.approval_rule: Only registry rows whose display_approved_pr is set are copied. For this panel that is the owner's waiver of 2026-10-24 (Jose, issue #31) and, for the quadratic fit shown since, the owner's decision in #80: the dates are fitted estimates shown before skeptic-red-team has reviewed them, and none of them is an approved end date. Every other fitted date, the straight line's included, stays in the registry as a log of unapproved dates (R-a).
track_record.passed_rule: passed = the named date is before today (2026-11-14, the build date). A fitted date that has passed is a failed forecast (R-b.1): drawn hollow.
track_record.claimed_rule: claimed_halfwidth_pct = half the 95% range that refit claimed (a past claim) as a percentage of the time the fit said remained (named date minus refit date); null when the fit is pinned to a grid edge or the range is unbounded above.
track_record.moved_rule: moved_next_pct = how far the named date moved by the next refit shown here, as a percentage of the time the fit said remained (the owner's '% error'); moved_latest_pct = the same against the latest refit shown; null when either fit is pinned.
track_record.ai_only_rule: ai_only = the AI-only fit at the same cut (no Kurzweil points): only whether its range is bounded and whether it is pinned to a grid edge are copied, never its date.
track_record.recession_rule: summaries: results/predictions/recession.csv for the same list and method, over every refit in the registry, not only the ones shown (r = days the named date moved per day that passed, unpinned refits only; NA if fewer than 5).

method_notes.calendar: refit at a calendar date with the releases dated before it; the open gap since the last release is a censored lower bound; the curve is quadratic in the log of the time left (since #80; the part7/part8 headline method was the straight line)
method_notes.release_cut: refit the day after each listed release (part8's held-out loop)

summaries.interval_method: Newey-West HAC, Bartlett kernel, lag ceil(sqrt(n)), n/(n-2) factor, t(n-2) 95%

card_range.rule: The omega card's range and the calendar's omega band: the list's last release on or before the refit day, plus the time the fit said remained times lower_mult and upper_mult. The multipliers are the 50% band (80% in the tooltip) of the quadratic fit's rolling backtest held-out errors in log remaining time (results/predictions/part8_rd_quad.json, calibrated_range.json, #40, #80), symmetric about the fit's own point, so the named date does not move: the card's date is the latest refit's named date. Owner's decision (#31, #80); not yet reviewed by our skeptic agent.
